base_rate_used.reference_class: PL teams sitting 3rd and about 6 points off the lead after 10 games that go on to win the title. From recall of PL history (approximate, not re-counted from a table): the champion was 6+ points off the lead after 10 games in only a handful of 33 completed seasons (e.g. Man United 1992-93 and 1995-96, Arsenal 1997-98, Man City 2013-14 and 2020-21), and any single club in that position converts roughly 1 time in 8

evidence: Table after matches played 2026-11-08 (MD10): Arsenal 27, Brighton 22, Man City 21 (7W 0D 3L, GF 21, GA 13, GD +8). City have gone from 7/7 wins and a 3-point lead on 2026-10-19 to 3rd and 6 points behind

The 7-0-3 record means all three defeats came in the last three league games: Villa 2-1 City (MW8), a MW9 defeat (inferred from the W-D-L record, opponent not checked) and Nott'm Forest 3-1 City on 2026-11-07

2026-11-07: Maresca said City could not match Forest's intensity and conceded two near-identical goals to Delap; Guehi and Gvardiol both asked to come off at half-time with knocks (two first-choice defenders doubtful)
New manager this season: Guardiola resigned, Enzo Maresca appointed 2026-06-29. Haaland still leads the scoring chart with 9

Sanction status: an independent commission found City guilty of 114 of 115 charges (reported 2026-09-25). No penalty has been announced. City lodged an appeal on 2026-10-01. On 2026-10-14 the football regulator chair said the appeal should be heard by mid or late January 2027; a ruling is due within 30 days of the hearing, so around February 2027. Sanctions are set in a separate confidential hearing; it is not confirmed that they would apply to the 2026-27 table, but the League wants the matter closed within the season. Commentators describe a heavy deduction (figures of 40+ points are speculation)
Resolution rule: a deduction applied before the final table is confirmed counts, so any sizeable in-season deduction takes City to ~0
questions.strongest_opposing_case: City had the best 7-game start in the league three weeks ago and still have the league's top scorer; a 6-point gap with 28 games left is two results, and City have closed bigger gaps on Arsenal in recent seasons. Three losses can be a new-manager blip plus two away trips. The sanction may well not land this season: the appeal ruling is not due before February, the penalty hearing is separate, City will contest the timetable, and a further challenge to the penalty could push any deduction into 2027-28. If the appeal succeeds the cloud lifts entirely. On that reading City deserve something near 0.18-0.20.
questions.reasoning_summary: Base 0.12 for a side 3rd and 6 points back after 10. Up for squad quality well above the typical 3rd-placed side (to ~0.17 on football alone). Down for three straight league defeats under a new manager and two defenders hurt (back to ~0.16). Then multiply by the chance no material deduction hits the 2026-27 table: I put the chance of an in-season deduction at about 0.35-0.40 (guilty verdict already in, appeal success unlikely, League wants in-season closure, but timing and separate penalty process are unconfirmed). 0.16 x ~0.62 = 0.10. The opposing case is real on timing but does not undo the form evidence; hold 0.10. Down from 0.48 on 2026-10-23.

base_rate_used.reference_class: PL leaders after 10 games. All leaders after 10 convert roughly half the time (about 17 of 33 seasons, approximate recall). Leaders with a cushion of 5+ points after 10 convert far more often: recalled cases Man United 1993-94, Chelsea 2005-06, Man City 2017-18, Liverpool 2019-20, Arsenal 2025-26 all won; Newcastle 1995-96 (4 clear) did not. Small n (~6), so shrink toward the all-leaders rate
base_rate_used.source: Premier League historical tables after matchday 10 (researcher recall, approximate count); 0.5 all-leaders rate blended with ~0.8-0.85 for 5+ point leaders, small-n shrunk

evidence: Table after matches played 2026-11-08 (MD10): Arsenal 1st, 27 pts (9W 0D 1L, GF 15, GA 5, GD +10), 5 clear of Brighton (22) and 6 clear of Man City (21)
Results since last dossier: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal (MW9, away win at a direct rival) and Arsenal 1-0 Hull on 2026-11-07 (Odegaard 72'); ninth win in ten
Arsenal are defending champions (won 2025-26 by 6 points over City) with the same manager; best defence in the league (5 conceded in 10)

Main rival of the last four seasons, Man City, has lost three straight league games and carries an unresolved guilty verdict on 114 charges that could bring an in-season deduction

questions.strongest_opposing_case: Nine wins from ten on 15 goals is a results run ahead of the underlying margins: a string of 1-0 wins regresses, and a side scoring 1.5 a game does not usually reach 85+ points. Twenty-eight games remain, a 5-point lead is under two results, Arsenal carry a full European schedule and have a history of spring fade-outs (2022-23, 2023-24). Brighton's goal difference says they may be the better team right now, and City at full strength with no sanction can still run off ten wins. On that reading 0.55-0.60 is fairer.
questions.reasoning_summary: Base 0.65 for a leader 5+ clear after 10. Up for being the defending champion with the best defence and an away win over Liverpool (+0.03). Up for the nearest historically credible chaser (City) being both out of form and exposed to a deduction (+0.04). Down for thin scoring margins and the Brighton goal-difference signal (-0.03). Net 0.69. The opposing case bites on margins, which is why this stays below 0.75 despite the lead. Up from 0.30 on 2026-10-23.

questions.reasoning_summary: Base ~0.62 for 1st plus 3rd after 10. Up because the leader has a 5-6 point cushion and is the defending champion (the pair is carried almost entirely by Arsenal). No extra credit for City beyond 0.10. Set = sum of members = 0.79, leaving 0.21 for the field (Brighton ~0.12, Liverpool 0.04, Chelsea ~0.02, others ~0.03). Essentially unchanged from 0.78 on 2026-10-23, but the split inside the pair has flipped.
